title: I challenged myself to build a whole weird game in 48 hours to see what AI could do. Meet Debride - A cozy tactile cleaning game with a grotesque twist
author: c11dp
selftext:
Hi Reddit! This weekend I challenged myself to build a whole game, end to end, in 48 hours, leaning heavily into AI to see what I could manage to put together. I'm pretty happy with the results. I'd like to introduce you to Debride! Debride is a cozy cleaning game where you pick and pluck away at a rampant alien infestation, ultimately making it all squeaky clean again. I was inspired by sensory picking toys, and feel like I've managed to capture that feeling digitally.

The game includes 3 different tools to unlock, as well as multiple pets and treats to feed them. This demo version includes the first 10 levels, and shows off a variety of organisms that you dissect and clean up with the help of your two coworkers: Maru and Doc.

You can play it right now for free on Itch.io: [https://c11dp.itch.io/debride](https://c11dp.itch.io/debride)

Basically everything you see was made using AI. I used Codex for art generation, ElevenLabs for SFX and music, and Claude Code to put it all together in Godot. I let Claude take a stab at writing the dialog based on a small story prompt, and tweaked it by hand to try and make it a little less "AI" sounding.

I hope you all enjoy!

comments.author: Ok_Advance8545
comments.body: Are all those flat images created by Codex, or did you also use 3D objects?

replies.author: c11dp
replies.body: They are flat images but generated in a way they can be sliced up and layered. They’re animated with a 2D tweening and spline system Claude Code set up which is how they are able to deform when dragged. Codex was prompted by Claude Code directly to make all of the art assets.

replies.author: Ok_Advance8545
replies.body: Oh, that's genius. It's really, really satisfying to play. i like it . It reminds me of some dental games I played as a kid.

replies.author: c11dp
replies.body: Thank you so much, and I’m glad you’re enjoying it! I had a lot of fun testing it, it scratches something in my brain haha
